thread:
ashley: Kicking off final PRD acceptance + rollback playbook for Dedicated v1.2 launch. Need clear SLO gates, canary thresholds, and step-by-step rollback/runbook. Can we finalize today?

mike: +1. I'll propose concrete SLO numbers and circuit-breaker thresholds. also need monitoring dashboards and a pager playbook.

jordan: FYI the runtime team added a KV-cache warmup phase in the canary; we should account for skewed latencies during first 10 min.

emily: Customer asks: predictable tail latency for short chat calls (<=256 tokens). They said p95 is most important. Also want SLA wording for Dedicated contracts.

ashley: Proposed acceptance gates (draft):
- Canary window: 60m rolling
- p50/p95/p99 targets for short requests (<=256 tokens): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms
- Error rate (5xx + model decode failures) <= 0.5% averaged over window
- No increase in cost-per-token > 15% vs baseline in canary
- No undetected quality regressions on eval prompt set (regression < 1%)
If any gate fails, trigger rollback playbook. Thoughts on these thresholds?

mike: Reasonable. Couple of clarifications:
- Use both absolute and relative checks: absolute p99 <= 300ms, and relative delta vs baseline <= +20% for p95/p99
- Error budget policy: if error rate > 0.5% for 5m OR sustained > 1.0% for 15m -> open incident, automatic canary pause and fallback to smaller quantized model variant (model-q4b)
- Circuit breaker: if tail latency (p99) increases > 50% vs baseline for 10m -> activate circuit-breaker -> route 30% traffic to fallback pool; if still bad after 5m -> 100% rollback

jordan: On warmup: first 10m will show elevated p95 due to KV cache misses. Suggest we have an initial "warmup exclusion": metrics only start evaluating acceptance after 10m, but keep an eye on error spikes immediately.

ashley: Good point. Update: canary = 70m total, with first 10m warmup (monitor-only). Acceptance window = last 60m.

emily: SLA wording suggestion for contracts: "Redwood Dedicated v1.2 aims to maintain p95 inference latency <= 120ms and availability >= 99.9% monthly. Where availability depends on successful completion of inference requests (HTTP 2xx). Credits apply when monthly availability < 99.9%." Need legal to confirm, but want the metrics mapped to what ops measures.

mike: Ops mapping: availability = 1 - (failed_requests / total_requests) where failed_requests = 5xx + timeout + deserialization errors. We'll add synthetic probes and agent-level heartbeats.

sasha: On quality/regressions: we'll run the eval suite (500 canonical prompts) in parallel for canary. Acceptance: no more than 1% of prompts degrade by > delta_score (we should define delta_score = -0.05 BLEU-ish / or -0.03 embedding-sim). If quality fails, do NOT rollback automatically; open a quality incident and hold rollout until triage.

ashley: Triage flow distinction:
- Reliability failures (errors/latency) -> automated fallback/rollback per playbook
- Quality regressions -> manual hold and rollback only after triage and consensus from ML/PD/Eng

mike: Draft rollback playbook (for infra team):
```
1) Detect: alert -> #incidents + pager
2) Pause canary traffic (deploy-bot pause-canary <deploy_id>)
3) Route traffic to fallback model pool (model-q4b) using routing rule "canary-fallback-<id>"
4) If fallback restores SLOs within 5m -> keep fallback and open postmortem
5) If not restored after fallback attempt -> full rollback to previous deployment image (deploy-bot rollback <deploy_id>)
6) Run smoke tests: /smoke/inference-short, /smoke/kv-cache
7) If smoke tests fail -> escalate to eng-oncall and hold customer communication
8) After rollback, collect traces, flamegraphs, and model decode logs and attach to incident ticket
```

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary start for release/dedicated-v1.2 at 1767890450 (70m window; warmup 10m) :rocket:

mike: Additions to playbook: automated runbook step to bump up autoscale headroom by +2 GPUs for 10m if p95 spikes with healthy error rate (helps backlog flush). Also add a token-cost monitor to avoid runaway cost.

jordan: Need to ensure the KV-cache warmup is visible in dashboards: add a chart with "cold-start p95" and an annotation when canary warmup period is active.

emily: Customer comms template (for success/failure):
- Success: "We completed the Dedicated v1.2 rollout canary; observed p95 <= 120ms and availability >= 99.95% in canary window. Rolling to 100% per schedule."
- Failure: "We paused the rollout due to increased error rate/latency. We're routing to fallback and investigating; we'll share a timeline in 60 minutes."

ashley: Edge cases to document in PRD:
- Gradual degradation where p95 is ok but p99 spikes -> our policy prefers tail safety: treat p99 regressions same as p95 if > 50% increase
- Token-length distribution shift from production customers -> may increase token compute cost; guard via cost delta check
- Intermittent model decode NaNs -> count as error and escalate immediately

sasha: For eval thresholds: we'll log per-example diffs and flag any semantic drift using embedding-sim < 0.88 as red. We'll attach a digest to the post-canary report.

mike: Where to store runbook? Add link to runbook in the PRD doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated-v1.2-runbook (placeholder). Also create a runbook snippet in ops-runbooks repo.

ashley: Next steps:
- mike: finalize playbook + add pager rules by EOD (1767891000)
- jordan: update dashboards + canary warmup annotation by EOD
- sasha: finalize eval thresholds and attach test harness to canary pipeline
- emily: draft SLA wording and comms templates for legal review
- I'll update PRD with final acceptance gates and link the runbook

mike: Will also add automated post-canary checklist that collects traces, perf profiles, and cost delta report to the release ticket.

emily: Thanks — once these are in PRD we can schedule the broader launch review.

ashley: Great. If anyone hits blockers ping me or drop in #product-async. Closing thread after we confirm EOD items. :white_check_mark:
